stories.h: Kenyan cult leader convicted over starvation deaths of 190 children
stories.dek: A Mombasa court found preacher Paul Mackenzie and 28 others guilty of murder over the Shakahola Forest deaths, with sentencing set for 6 November.

stories.h: Saudi Arabia postpones 'Davos in the Desert' to 2027 amid Houthi attacks
stories.dek: The Future Investment Initiative, due in Riyadh from 26 to 29 October, has been pushed back with no new date set.

stories.h: Drone strike on Abyei market kills at least 153 people
stories.dek: The toll from Monday's attack in the disputed Sudan-South Sudan border zone more than doubled as fires slowed recovery of bodies.

stories.h: Alberta voters reject a path toward independence from Canada
stories.dek: Roughly three in four voters backed staying in Canada, a boost for Prime Minister Mark Carney, though separatists say the movement will continue.

stories.h: Japan launches probe to bring back samples from Mars's moon Phobos
stories.dek: The MMX spacecraft lifted off on an H3 rocket and reached its planned orbit, starting a mission meant to return samples in 2031.

stories.h: Oslo talks on Ukraine end without a deal as Witkoff heads to Putin
stories.dek: Zelenskyy met US envoy Steve Witkoff and European leaders in Norway, with Washington calling the talks constructive but no agreement reached.

stories.h: Meta posts record revenue, but a legal charge and AI spending cut profit
stories.dek: Third-quarter revenue rose 26 percent to $64.6 billion while free cash flow turned negative and the company announced a new class of non-voting shares.

stories.h: Tesla beats profit forecast as deliveries top estimates but margins stay thin
stories.dek: Revenue was flat at $28.05 billion, and AI and robotics spending pushed operating income down 56 percent.

stories.h: Iran says seven ships hit in Hormuz as US and Europe weigh next move
stories.dek: The Revolutionary Guard's claim of its highest single-day toll in the strait is disputed by the US, while ministers urge diplomacy and Washington hints at strikes.

stories.h: US measles cases pass 4,500 as the country's 2026 total doubles last year's
stories.dek: CDC data show 4,588 confirmed cases, though growth slowed to 4 percent for the week.

stories.h: Israel locks down Hebron after attack kills two soldiers days before election
stories.dek: Netanyahu ordered the West Bank city sealed and prepared wider closures as the army launched a multi-day operation and arrests mounted.

stories.h: Louvre, Orsay and Grand Palais shut as Paris braces for protests
stories.dek: France's culture ministry closed leading museums on Saturday, and Art Basel Paris cancelled its weekend programme after opening to the public on Friday.

stories.h: Climate plans from 132 countries fall short on protecting health, new scorecard finds
stories.dek: The Global Climate and Health Alliance ranks Colombia first and finds India, Japan and New Zealand at the bottom.

stories.h: Hundreds of thousands march across France as nearly 1,000 are arrested
stories.dek: A week after rioting and looting, Saturday's protests over living costs passed with clashes in several cities under a 70,000-strong police deployment.

stories.h: Brewers edge Rays 3-2 in World Series opener after overturned double play
stories.dek: Milwaukee led from the first inning, and a replay reversal let Tampa Bay score in the ninth before the Brewers closed it out.

stories.h: World may have only a month or two of usable oil reserves, analysts warn
stories.dek: With Brent near $111 and the US reserve at its lowest since 1982, a renewed Hormuz closure would hit stockpiles already drawn down.

stories.h: Brazil votes in knife-edge runoff between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro
stories.dek: Final polls show a near dead heat as nearly 160 million eligible voters choose between the veteran president and the son of the jailed ex-president.

stories.h: Serbia votes in snap election as Vučić faces a student-led challenge
stories.dek: The president turned prime-ministerial candidate leads some polls, but others put the student list ahead after two years of protests.
